newsitem.title: USA: Union negotiatiors recess GM talks for the day.
newsitem.headline: Union negotiatiors recess GM talks for the day.

text.p: Negotiators for the United Auto Workers have left General Motors Corp. headquarters for the day and will resume talks on a new labour deal starting about 8:30 a.m. EST Tuesday, a union spokesman said Monday.
Some union bargainers had originally been scheduled to return to GM later Monday for more talks, but those plans changed, said Reg McGhee, a UAW spokesman.
After a morning news conference, the whole union negotiating team returned to GM for a few hours, said McGhee, who added that he did not know if there were any discussions with GM bargainers.

Union and company officials are trying to come up with a new three-year contract covering the 215,000 UAW members at GM's U.S. operations. Ford Motor Co. and Chrysler Corp. already have new labour contracts with the union.
UAW President Stephen Yokich said Monday he will continue talks with the automaker and has no plans to call a strike, even though a contract expiration deadline expired at midnight Sunday.
The two sides are wrangling over job security and outsourcing -- the practice of farming out work to non-GM suppliers, which can often perform the work more cheaply with non-union workers.
